Startup environment variables seed config.json only when it cannot be loaded; later restarts can ignore changed values. A corrupt config can trigger reseeding, so recovery is not a credential-rotation contract. A reachable UI or live container does not prove an approved project is running or uploads have completed.

Read-only OCI inspection on 2026-10-03 verified immutable manifest/config, compressed layer SHA-256, and later-layer overlays/whiteouts. run-warrior3 imports seesaw.script.run_warrior; final library-copy layer direct_url.json pins seesaw bb6673d27a8717e13efe5d7deb3628349cd08585 and six runtime source files byte-match that revision. Earlier reviewed seesaw 699b0d2 is not the installed revision. The unpinned clone's installed warrior-code2 Git ref is 465aa2223a9d6d863f3e8ff173eaf8bfb5fbd0d5; labels alone would not establish either dependency.

The publisher healthcheck reads /index.html on port 8001; it proves only that the web frontend responds. Projects and seeded config.json live in the container's Warrior projects directory; retain only reviewed project-owned storage, and do not mistake temporary downloads for an archive or backup.

The shared recipe supports only explicitly selected idle mode: nickname, selected_project=none, concurrency=1, HQ registration/update traffic, CPU 1 and memory 512 MiB. The owner requires private writable UID-1000 configuration and exact resume validation before controlled start. No disk quota, HQ bandwidth cap or network destination firewall is implemented. Archival workload approval and acceptance remain separate and unsupported; idle readiness is not zero external work.

The current manual-job contract permits fixed publisher version probes only for restic, Borgmatic and Renovate. security: The container actively downloads and uploads Archive Team work; require explicit consent to the selected project, outbound traffic, resource use, and destination policy before start.

SELECTED_PROJECT=none is not an offline bootstrap: the upstream runner registers and sends updates to Warrior HQ during startup. Approve those external writes separately, or establish and verify an inert bootstrap with fail-closed egress before normal shared apply.

Keep the port 8001 web control interface private. Configure its documented HTTP_USERNAME and HTTP_PASSWORD together before exposing it to other users; do not assume it has an administrator account by default.
Do not include the recommended Watchtower Docker-socket mount in a shared Compose project. Review image updates as a separate scoped action.

Keep the RPC token out of process arguments, logs, Compose manifests, and ordinary reports.

A locally managed branch must bind an existing credential JSON and fresh provider account/tunnel identity with config_src=local to one owner-selected frontend/hostname, disable WARP routing, retain a final http_status:404 rule, inspect provider route inventories, and separately approve DNS/TLS/auth ownership before startup. pitfalls: A PDF toolbox is not a durable document archive or backup.
security: Process sensitive PDFs only on a trusted private route.

name: Syncthing

lifecycle.note: Official Docker image and configuration routes checked; shared setup lacks a safe first-GUI-credential/API-key bootstrap and peer-network acceptance.

acceptance.description: Set static GUI username and generated password through an authorized configuration route, then prove that the saved password authenticates and an unauthenticated GUI request is rejected.
Read the generated key from this exact owned config, save it privately, and verify an authenticated REST read; do not claim setup from the unauthenticated health endpoint.
After approving exact device and folder shares, verify a real peer connection and authorized file round-trip; a running GUI alone is insufficient.
Restart only the owned Compose project and recheck saved GUI login, API key, and peer/folder state.

pitfalls: Synchronization propagates deletions and is not a backup.
An unpublished peer/discovery port or container bridge can leave the GUI running while device sync is unusable.
The documented offline credential generator and API-key-protected REST configuration need an exact private-file/container-operation primitive before shared setup can claim readiness.
security: Authenticate and restrict the GUI before any non-loopback exposure; the official Docker image listens on all container interfaces by default.
Protect the device private key and API key; review each device and folder share separately.

name: Tailscale

lifecycle.note: The experimental portless recipe starts only userspace tailscaled with owned persistent state. Enrollment and private Serve activation are separately gated; intended-client ACL and restart acceptance remain unverified.

acceptance.description: After separate enrollment approval, read Running status, expected tailnet suffix and the stable node identity; reject SSH, subnet and exit routing preferences.
After separate Serve approval, read back the exact selected same-owner frontend HTTPS proxy, with no Funnel or additional routes; intended-client ACL allow/deny remains separate.
Verify authorized and denied clients against the intended route and prove it is absent from the ordinary internet; local status alone is not client acceptance.
After scoped restart, prove the same stable node identity, saved Serve route and ACL restrictions persist without re-enrollment.

pitfalls: A running container or local daemon status does not prove the node is registered and authorized in the intended tailnet. TS_ENABLE_HEALTH_CHECK exposes /healthz, but HTTP 200 proves only that the node has at least one tailnet IP, not intended-client access or ACL enforcement.

The portless private-connector recipe publishes no host frontend and joins only the shared owner frontend bridge plus its private network. It starts /usr/local/bin/tailscaled directly instead of containerboot, so credential import and Compose apply do not implicitly enroll or activate Serve.

The pinned containerboot rejects TS_DEST_IP and TS_EXPERIMENTAL_DEST_DNS_NAME when TS_USERSPACE is enabled. These forwarding settings cannot replace a reviewed private Serve configuration without separately approved kernel-network privileges.

The daemon writes /var/lib/tailscale/tailscaled.state into its owned persistent volume. Enrollment must use a non-ephemeral owner-issued key and a reviewed retention/revocation policy; local node status cannot prove the key's remote policy. Never copy the key payload into a Compose environment file.

Serve is private while Funnel is public; they are different approval classes. TS_SERVE_CONFIG can configure either, so any imported Serve configuration needs an explicit no-Funnel review and an exact owned upstream target. Upstream requires a directory bind, not an individual file bind, to detect configuration updates.

A reusable private-connector contract must bind the selected same-owner app/service/port, persistent node identity, owner-file enrollment and ACL owner into approval. Reject Funnel, subnet routes, exit-node settings and SSH; verify tailscale status --json and tailscale serve status --json without claiming intended-client access from local status alone.
security: Enrollment requires an owner-supplied auth-key file kept outside catalog data and command arguments. The pinned tailscale up CLI consumes --auth-key=file:/run/secrets/auth-key directly; shared import saves owner-only bytes, while the ordinary recipe starts only a daemon and performs no enrollment.

Default userspace networking does not route the host or sibling containers. Kernel networking requires separately approved /dev/net/tun and NET_ADMIN; subnet routes, exit-node use, Serve, and public Funnel each need separate review.

name: Tdarr

lifecycle.note: Pinned server/internal-node Compose candidate with a source-backed 2.92.01 first-owner and API-key adapter. Exact frontend request contracts are recorded in bootstrap-source.md; live authentication, node connectivity, and restart acceptance remain unverified.

acceptance.description: The pinned headless adapter registers the first admin with the saved password and verifies a fresh login and admin role; independently verify the private web UI.
The pinned headless adapter saves and inserts one owned API key, then verifies inventory with that key; independently verify node connectivity before enabling workers.
Enable workers only after separate approval of writable library behavior; first test a copied file and preserve its source.
Restart only the owned service and recheck administrator login, API-key access, and saved configuration.

pitfalls: A bad transcode policy can replace source media; test on copies and preserve recoverable originals.
The documented seededApiKey setting creates a key, not a first-admin identity. The headless adapter separately registers the first admin, verifies login, and saves an owned API key before insertion.
Port 8266 is the server/API listener and is not published by the shared recipe; only the web UI is mapped to loopback.
The internal node starts with zero configured workers; approve library write behavior and test on copies before enabling transcoding.
security: Limit worker access to owner-selected libraries and approve GPU or device access explicitly.
Keep the first-user setup screen private; auth=true does not pre-create an administrator or close registration.

name: Technitium DNS Server

lifecycle.note: Broader authoritative and recursive DNS feature set than a simple filter.

acceptance.description: Authenticate the generated admin password and read back the authenticated user profile.
After separate LAN owner approval, expose TCP and UDP 53 and verify DNS from a LAN client and fallback routing.
Restart only the owned Compose project and verify administrator login and saved settings.

pitfalls: A broad DNS feature set increases configuration and recovery scope.
The shared recipe publishes only the loopback web console. DNS on TCP/UDP 53 requires a separate LAN owner and cutover plan.
security: Separate public authoritative service from private recursion and administration.

name: Tracearr

lifecycle.note: Pinned v2.6.0 source supplies a shared three-service recipe and checkpointed Better Auth first-owner/public API-key adapter. Required email is an explicit setup input. PostgreSQL 18 remains experimental and fresh-volume-only. Source/synthetic validation is not fresh-image, restart, media-server, or Homarr acceptance.

acceptance.description: Create only the first owner with the reviewed email and generated password; verify a fresh username login and owner identity.
Generate one durable public API key only when absent, recover by inventory after lost responses, and verify authenticated public API access.
Connect only a separately approved media-server endpoint and credential; account setup does not enroll or download media.
Restart only the owned project and reverify owner login and API-key access.

pitfalls: Session analytics are not a replacement for service readiness or host monitoring.
The standard image requires TimescaleDB, not plain PostgreSQL, and a secret-bearing DATABASE_URL.
The current official pg18 Compose example calls PostgreSQL 18 experimental and new-install-only; never reuse an existing data volume with it.
The bundled local-owner adapter requires a reviewed email, refuses an existing uncheckpointed owner or claim-code setup, and never repeats an uncertain signup or API-key rotation.
Owner and API-key setup does not enroll a media server, fetch media, configure notifications, or prove Homarr integration or restart persistence.
security: Treat session history, user identities, IP data, and media-server API access as sensitive.

name: Traefik

lifecycle.note: Private ping plus Basic-authenticated exact GET-only management paths support the native Homarr source contract. The fixed middleware username is control access, not a created account. No Docker provider/socket, dashboard, application ingress, or TLS is enabled. Existing ping-only owners need a separately supported recipe transition. Source fixtures are not live acceptance.

acceptance.description: GET /ping on the saved loopback origin returns 200; this proves only the Traefik process responds.

Verify anonymous denial, saved Basic credentials and the exact GET-only router. Credentials provide control access, not a user account. Old owners need a reviewed recipe transition; no automatic migration.
Separately approve and verify a real route, DNS/TLS/80/443/auth owner, and Docker API boundary if Docker discovery is chosen; this recipe provides none.
Restart the exact owned Compose project and verify the approved route and certificate state after ingress is configured separately.

pitfalls: The recipe never enables insecure API/dashboard access. Control-interface credentials do not create Traefik user records; existing owners are not silently migrated or given replacement credentials.
security: Protect the Docker API and authenticate the dashboard.

name: Transmission

lifecycle.note: Active upstream client with daemon and RPC deployment options.

acceptance.description: Verify unauthenticated RPC is denied, then authenticate with the saved admin password and read the pinned session version through the CSRF-protected RPC endpoint.
Verify the selected /downloads bind and configured download directory before any authorized transfer.
Peer TCP/UDP port publication and downloader VPN routing remain separate approvals; VPN acceptance needs a tunnel-break fail-closed test.
Restart only this owned service and repeat authenticated RPC and storage checks.

pitfalls: This private recipe does not publish the TCP/UDP peer port or establish a VPN kill switch. Incoming peers and VPN-safe downloading require separately approved work.
security: Keep the authenticated RPC/WebUI bound to loopback; separately approve peer-port publication and downloader VPN routing.

name: Umami

lifecycle.note: Privacy-oriented analytics; consent obligations remain jurisdiction-specific.

acceptance.description: On the exact private origin, prove the seeded administrator identity, rotate its password once, verify the generated password and rejection of the seed.
Configure an approved site and prove a real event is collected; login alone is not analytics acceptance.
Restart this exact project and verify the rotated administrator and previously collected data remain available.
Restore PostgreSQL in isolation before claiming backup verification.

pitfalls: Self-hosting does not remove consent, retention, or data-governance duties.
The seeded administrator is reachable on the selected loopback origin until the separately approved password-rotation setup completes; never expose it more broadly before rotation is verified.
security: Keep administration private, change the seeded admin/umami password immediately, generate unique APP_SECRET and TWO_FACTOR_ENCRYPTION_KEY values, and minimize collected visitor data.

name: Unbound

lifecycle.note: Headless DNS component; the cited container is community-maintained, not published by NLnet Labs.

acceptance.description: From the selected private client, query an external name through both UDP and TCP port 5335 and verify the answer; the image healthcheck alone observes an open port.
Only after a separate DNS-owner approval, review exact bind address, client ACL, TCP/UDP ports, fallback DNS, and prove no public recursion.
Restart only the owned Compose project and repeat private TCP and UDP DNS queries.

pitfalls: An open recursive resolver creates abuse and availability risk.
security: Restrict recursion to intended clients and keep controls private.

name: Uptime Kuma

lifecycle.note: Pinned v2.5.5 shared first-owner Socket.IO setup saves a nonexpiring metrics-only API key. Key creation globally replaces administrator Basic auth on /metrics with API-key Basic auth; it is not a general management API or MCP token. Workload and restart acceptance remain separate.

acceptance.description: Skip the database wizard with pinned SQLite configuration, create the first owner through Socket.IO polling with exact reviewed application events, and verify login with the saved password. The shared adapter is enabled but still needs fresh-instance acceptance.
Create or select a monitor and confirm its expected state through an owner-authenticated readback.
Restart this exact project and confirm its account and monitor remain available.

pitfalls: Its data path requires POSIX locks and is not supported on NFS.
security: Protect the admin UI and notification credentials.
Creating an API key globally changes /metrics authentication from administrator Basic auth to API-key Basic auth. The owned nonexpiring key is metrics-only, not a general API or MCP token.

name: Valkey

lifecycle.note: Official image identified; private unauthenticated shared Compose readiness is available, but peer compatibility, authenticated access, and live acceptance remain unverified.

acceptance.description: valkey-cli PING from the exact running Valkey container returns PONG; this proves only local service readiness, not peer access or authentication.
From each separately reviewed trusted peer, verify private TCP access and its documented Valkey compatibility; reject unknown or untrusted peers.
Restart the exact owned project and verify a deliberately created probe key remains when persistence is required for the selected workload.
For durable queue use, restore a consistent Valkey backup into an isolated instance and verify the intended key data.

pitfalls: Do not assume Redis and Valkey versions are interchangeable for every application.
The official image has no documented generated-password-file bootstrap; unauthenticated PING or container liveness does not prove safe peer access or a secure deployment.
security: Keep TCP port 6379 loopback-only on the host and restrict the shared Compose network to trusted applications. The no-account recipe has no authentication; require separately reviewed ACL or requirepass configuration before any untrusted peer or broader exposure.

name: Vaultwarden

lifecycle.note: Unofficial Bitwarden-compatible server, not the vendor server. The pinned shared recipe installs persistent storage with registration and invitations closed. Canonical HTTPS and encrypted official-client enrollment remain separate gates; the standalone owner is retained for existing installations.

acceptance.description: Read the exact owned TLS origin and verify API environment URLs match its approved DOMAIN; separately prove intended-client DNS and CA trust.

After separate bounded signup approval, create only the selected email account with the compatible official client and the saved generated master password; verify fresh login and decrypted vault unlock.
Read effective registration policy after closure; persisted overrides, whitelist and invitations require separate inspection. Do not infer closure from Compose environment alone.
Restart only this owner and verify fresh login and decrypted vault access; encrypted export and isolated restore remain separate recovery gates before real vault migration.

pitfalls: Compatibility and recovery are higher consequence than an ordinary web app.
The built-in admin page is disabled without ADMIN_TOKEN; enabling it is separate from creating a vault owner and must not substitute for HTTPS or signup controls.

SIGNUPS_ALLOWED=false closes ordinary registration, but organization invitations and admin invitations have separate behavior. A nonempty SIGNUPS_DOMAINS_WHITELIST and persisted config.json overrides must also be checked before claiming registration closure.

The pinned server reads secret settings through documented source-level NAME_FILE support and rejects simultaneous NAME and NAME_FILE inputs. ADMIN_TOKEN may contain an Argon2id PHC hash, but enabling server administration is separate from creating or unlocking a vault account; keep it disabled unless explicitly needed.

The shared recipe generates one owner-only master-password file but does not bind it into the server or enable ADMIN_TOKEN. Vault account registration requires the Bitwarden client's KDF, authentication hash and wrapped encryption key; a generic email/password POST or an admin login is not a compatible first-owner bootstrap.

Applied private HTTPS and a stable canonical DOMAIN are prerequisites, not first-owner evidence. Shared setup still needs a separately pinned official-client enrollment and decrypted-unlock boundary. Keep the existing standalone signup/closure/recovery gate until that boundary exists; server health, a password-grant token, or an ADMIN_TOKEN session must never satisfy vault-account readiness.
security: Require a verified private HTTPS origin before account creation or client use; keep administration private, registration closed outside a bounded first-account gate, and recovery material protected.
Do not treat the shared loopback HTTP origin or a healthy container as web-vault acceptance.

name: Vector

lifecycle.note: The private recipe only routes Vector's own logs to stdout; real telemetry needs a separately reviewed source and sink.

acceptance.description: GET /health on the exact loopback origin returns HTTP 200 and an ok:true body; this proves only Vector is initialized and serving.
After separately approved source and sink configuration, prove one authorized event traverses the intended route without sensitive-data leakage.
Restart the exact owned project and verify the reviewed topology and event route still work.

pitfalls: Broad Docker or host log access can collect unintended sensitive content.
The self-only recipe does not collect host or application logs; a running process or healthy API does not establish real ingestion.
security: Redact credentials and personal data before routing telemetry.
The unauthenticated observability API must remain on loopback or another private trusted network when enabled.

name: VictoriaMetrics

lifecycle.note: Candidate metrics backend; edition and topology need review.

acceptance.description: Read the single-node health and build-info endpoints and verify the pinned version.
Query the explicitly enabled self-scrape metrics to verify ingestion and querying.
Restart the exact owned project and verify self-scraped metrics remain queryable.

pitfalls: Prometheus compatibility does not make retention and scaling choices identical.
security: Keep ingestion and query endpoints private unless authenticated.

name: What's Up Docker

lifecycle.note: Pinned 9.1.0 remote TLS watcher recipe requires explicit endpoint/container/mode choices, imported owner-issued CA/certificate/key files and a separately approved fresh remote Docker connection before every start. Management mode explicitly grants host-wide Docker control, not read-only authority; inventory mode remains blocked without verified deny-write policy. Setup verifies the saved Basic administrator, anonymous denial and exact single-container image against the approved Docker engine. Live TLS/ACL acceptance, current scan freshness and restart persistence remain unverified. No socket or registry-only mode is provided.

pitfalls: An available tag is not proof that an upgrade is compatible, backed up, or reversible.

Pinned 9.1.0 registerWatchers creates a default local Docker watcher when none is configured. Available watcher providers are Docker, Kubernetes, Nomad, and Swarm; registry providers look up image updates for watcher-supplied inventory and do not offer a standalone registry-only mode. A web-only Compose container without an approved watcher would not perform useful monitoring.
Do not expose raw Docker TCP port 2375 publicly or treat Docker socket :ro as an API permission boundary.
security: Do not mount the Docker socket directly; a read-only bind mount does not make Docker API operations read-only. Upstream recommends a Docker socket proxy with CONTAINERS, IMAGES, INFO, VERSION, EVENTS, and PING reads enabled and mutating operations denied. The proxy requires separate exact socket approval and a WUD-only network; never publish its Docker API port by default.

Keep the web UI private, seed WUD_AUTH_ADMIN_USER and WUD_AUTH_ADMIN_PASSWORD at the narrow apply boundary, and persist WUD state. Do not put the bootstrap password in catalog data or an ordinary report.

Pinned authenticated POST /api/profile/tokens accepts name and read scopes and returns rawSecret only once; inventory cannot recover it. Any future adapter must checkpoint before creation, save privately, and refuse duplicate creation after an uncertain response. Bearer verification also updates token lastUsedAt and needs an explicit mutation approval.

WUD_AUTH_ADMIN_USER with PASSWORD or HASH updates the matching user's credentials and administrator role on startup. Plan this as ongoing declarative credential ownership, not an empty-database-only seed. Homarr's pinned native WUD client uses saved Basic username/password on /api/containers; a personal token is not required for that client.

name: ZeroTier

lifecycle.note: The official stable container tag is 1.14.2. The shared recipe bootstraps a container-local identity and native API token with separately reviewed NET_ADMIN and tun authority; enrollment remains owner-selected and unverified.

acceptance.description: Inside the exact saved container, reject anonymous service and controller reads, authenticate the saved native token, and checkpoint the stable node address and public identity.
Require empty local memberships and controller network inventory. Enrollment, controller authorization and route activation need separately reviewed ownership and approval.
After separately approved enrollment, verify assigned addresses and permitted/denied peer reachability; this container-local node does not provide host or sibling-app routing.
After a scoped restart, prove the same saved node identity and API token persist; local first-run proof does not establish restart acceptance.

pitfalls: Virtual LAN reachability can expose services beyond their host bind assumptions.
A successful join or running container is not network acceptance. Verify listnetworks reports OK and an assigned address after controller authorization, then test peer reachability.
Persist /var/lib/zerotier-one across upgrades to preserve node identity; keep identity.secret and authtoken.secret private.

The userspace libzt sockets SDK requires application integration and is not a drop-in unprivileged network sidecar for arbitrary shared services. The localhost service API token and the owner's Central authorization token are separate credentials.

The recipe creates no networks and joins none. Native identity and controller API readback is bootstrap readiness only; controller choice, network creation, membership authorization, assigned addresses and peer routes remain pending.

The owner-volume retains identity and controller data. Resume requires the same saved token and node identity; unknown or changed ownership must be inspected, not reset. UPnP/NAT-PMP mapping and in-container software updates are disabled.
security: Review network membership, routes, and controller ownership before joining; a network ID alone does not authorize a node.

The pinned official image needs NET_ADMIN and /dev/net/tun through the source-bound tun-net-admin approval. It uses its own bridge namespace, not host networking, and does not grant host or sibling-service routing.

The native management token is generated once into the owner-private file and supplied through the documented ZEROTIER_API_SECRET environment. Docker operators can inspect this token; it is not a local admin password or a Central API credential.
